instructions: The night before, or at least 4 hours ahead: rinse 1 1/2 cups of jasmine rice under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Transfer it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes. Spread the rice on a baking sheet to cool, then refrigerate it.
Pat the shrimp dry. Sprinkle the salt and pepper over them.
Peel the outer layers off the lemongrass and slice the bottom 4 inches of each stalk very thinly. Thinly slice the onion. Tear the lime leaves into pieces. Cut the lime in half.
In a small bowl, stir together 3 tbsp tom yum paste, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar and 2 tbsp of water. Break up any clumps in the cold rice with your hands.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the shrimp in one layer and cook for 1 minute per side, until pink. Transfer them to a plate.
Add the remaining 2 tbsp oil to the wok. Add the onion, lemongrass and lime leaves and stir for 2 minutes, until the onion softens and it smells fragrant.
Add the peas and stir for 1 minute.
Turn the heat to high. Add the rice and press it against the wok with the back of a spatula, then stir. Repeat for 3 minutes, until the rice is hot and the grains are loose.
Pour in the tom yum mixture and stir for 2 minutes, until every grain is coated.
Return the shrimp to the wok. Take it off the heat and squeeze in the juice of half the lime.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the other half of the lime, cut into wedges.
advance_prep_notes: cook and chill the rice the night before, or at least 4 hours ahead
method_notes: The lead is a Thai fried rice with shrimp, lemongrass, lime leaves, peas, fish sauce and lime. It builds its chili paste from scratch, which is not a 30-minute job, so this uses jarred tom yum paste, as the lead's own store-bought option and two other sources do (The Not So Creative Cook, Wok & Kin). The sources agree on day-old rice and cooking the shrimp first. The tom yum paste brand needs to be gluten-free, so check the label. Total time is 30 minutes once the rice is cooked and chilled.
